findings.title: Freeze the exact deterministic sampler and null-vector construction
findings.observation: The master seed and canonical array hashing are specified, but the digest-to-uniform-range rule is not: full-256-bit rejection below floor(2^256/q)*q and masked-bit rejection are different deterministic samplers satisfying the prose. Exact counter placement/start, range conventions, null coefficient domains and canonical nullspace-coordinate sampling are also unbound. The conditioned-null rule says to generate up to 100 hash-seeded vectors in a kernel without freezing the kernel basis/order or law on its coordinates. The unconditioned support-random wording should explicitly distinguish a vector with at least one nonzero coordinate from a vector with every supported coefficient nonzero. Finally instance_key includes arm, so null/instance generation must specify the arm-independent projection that guarantees identical generator bytes across solvers.
findings.why_it_matters: Different faithful implementations can produce different nulls, unavailable-null slots and rho schedules from the same frozen master seed. The current statement that every strategy and sample law is already frozen is stronger than the definitions. This is a reproducibility/design gap, not a demonstrated bias or failed scientific result.
findings.required_change: Add an immutable sampling addendum before implementation approval: exact byte-to-integer endianness/range/rejection threshold and counter placement, domain arrays for each draw, canonical support/constraint/kernel basis orders, coordinate distribution for kernel draws, and an arm-independent instance/control key. Preserve existing counts, first-accepted selection, 100/1024 limits and unavailable outcomes; do not silently choose after examining scientific outputs.
findings.minimal_discriminating_check: A later authorized benign QA fixture should reproduce hand-derived hash-to-range and coefficient-vector examples byte-for-byte in independent implementations. No such check was run here.

findings.title: Resolve the degree-null requirement without calling random coefficients semi-regular
findings.observation: RQ-PFDR declares a support-matched semi-regular null mandatory. The design deliberately does not assume semi-regularity for either null, but supplies no operational semi-regularity/reference-rank criterion or explicit source-applicability decision replacing or retaining that prerequisite. Also the conditioned null fixes the entire allowed zero set. With the frozen Boolean and membership equations, the design radicality lemma implies the original and conditioned-null ideals are equal in the same coordinate ring. Thus this is a same-ideal presentation perturbation, useful for studying discovery cost, but it does not destroy the coordinate-algebra structure whose sparse representation H1 proposes to exploit.
findings.why_it_matters: The design correctly avoids a false semi-regularity assertion. It must equally avoid treating this different null as having discharged the literal source-question degree requirement or treating persistence of ideal-intrinsic sparsity under an identical-ideal perturbation as an independent null test of that sparsity. This does not invalidate a matched finite solver-cost comparison.
findings.required_change: Through an additive Coordinator-approved applicability record, state which question each null tests, explicitly identify the conditioned arm as a same-ideal presentation control, and either define the appropriate support-matched generic/relative semi-regular reference with its assumptions and rejection criteria or retain the RQ degree-null obligation as unmet and exclude the affected degree/null claim from promotion. If a same-count/different-zero-set control is desired, preregister it separately; do not relabel existing fixed-zero-set rows or waive a required control by implication.
findings.minimal_discriminating_check: Manual protocol check: use the Boolean quotient description to compare the vanishing coordinates of I and I_null; identical surviving coordinates force the same ideal. No numerical nulls or field systems were generated.

findings.title: Define a disjoint stage-to-metric map for the H1 overhead inequality
findings.observation: H1 uses W_check and W_reduce and refers to the same frozen stage tags, while the cost model names broad stages without a total disjoint mapping to these two submetrics. Exact total W_field is defined, but assigning frontier-rank elimination, support scoring, source-witness reduction, commutator construction and root-eigenspace elimination to reduction versus checking versus another stage can change saved_reduction and extra_checking without changing total work.
findings.why_it_matters: The primary total-cost ratio can still be measured honestly, but H1 is a separate preregistered quantitative prediction and must not depend on a later tagging choice. This finding concerns the submetric definition only; it does not assert omitted total work.
findings.required_change: Freeze a stage/operation ownership table defining W_check and W_reduce for both algorithms and all fallbacks. State inclusions/exclusions, separate producer internal acceptance from independent verification, forbid double counting, and retain all remaining work in other total-cost stages. Bind the table into the reviewed specification/addendum before scoring any scientific case.
findings.minimal_discriminating_check: An authorized later meter QA should reconcile every operation in a small hand-defined trace into exactly one total stage and the declared H1 projections. This reviewer ran no meter checks.

findings.title: Make the resultant-loop O branch explicit
findings.observation: The actual ideal explicitly uses X1-X2 for m=2,R=O and S3 for m=3,R=O. The scheduled resultant_label_loop includes O, but its baseline prose names S3 for m=2 and S4 for m=3 without an exceptional-target override. Taken literally this requests an affine target coordinate that O does not have.
findings.required_change: State that the loop specializes the actual F selected by original_ideal.F, with explicit O branches using the lower-arity polynomials, preserving the same admitted-label enumeration and group filtering. This is a textual consistency repair; it does not require a changed panel or imply a source-formula failure.

findings.title: Specify the algebra structure in the finite formalization target
findings.observation: The general certificate gives a vector-space identification with K^B and a transported multiplication law. Writing R/I ~= K^B without stating that law can be misread as an isomorphism to the coordinatewise product algebra, which does not follow for general nonradical border certificates. The separately scheduled dual-number control is a concrete boundary already present in this design.
findings.required_change: Describe K^B first as a vector space with multiplication induced by the certified maps. Claim a product of copies of F_p only after the Boolean/split-radical lemma, indexed by satisfying assignments. The existing certificate argument and root-recovery procedure already support this distinction; no formal build occurred.

protocol_checks.assessment: Prime testing and exact point counts are defined prospectively; nonsingularity, prime-order subgroup and trace restrictions are explicit. The bit alphabet is enforced in F_p. Interval injectivity uses 2^s<p; actual rational-lift membership is independently encoded. Matched-random bases use a charged bijective label lookup. No carry or Weil-descent identity is silently assumed.

The proposed checker recomputes the complete original-ring border, checks every column/commutator/cyclic basis identity, expands each border-to-source witness and checks original-generator annihilation/reduction. This supplies the two containment directions and prevents a root/dimension oracle from certifying a wrong ideal. The zero algebra has a separate explicit unit witness. The result is protocol-level soundness analysis only.

Manual reasoning through the specified product-of-fields quotient shows that adding membership and summation equations discards non-satisfying assignments without introducing nilpotents or extension-field roots. Sequential invariant-subspace splits must retain all leaves and their dimensions. Digit roots decode injectively, but signed point solutions are counted separately and require all lifts and group checks.

The prescribed noncommuting fixture must fail its displayed commutator, even though individual Boolean annihilators hold. The one-root substitute for (d^2-d) fails border membership at d=1; empty matrices cannot replace a unit witness. Wrong coordinate action is distinct from abstract algebra dimension, and the dual-number/split pair tests the nonradical boundary. These are manual checks of proposed controls, not executed checker passes.

The primary ratio includes matched public-input costs, failed discovery/fallback, independent checking and complete recovery. Shared costs use fixed denominators and exact rational allocations; calibration is charged to held-out targets. Program totals retain null/QA/diagnostic costs separately. CPU, resident memory and storage are separate; descriptive curve-block summaries assert no population coverage. F3 remains necessary for the separate H1 submetrics.

Full ordinary-ring columns, consecutive-degree checks, generator-certificate bounds and same-base yields avoid output-degree or quotient-dimension substitutions. The design claims neither a theoretical regularity value nor an ECDLP exponent. F2 leaves the specific semi-regular-null/source admission question unresolved.
